history.summary: Mel Pazhani Murugan Temple sits atop Mayiladumkunnu hill near Mayanad/Meenchanda, about 10 km from Kozhikode city. CSV TOWN CORRECTED: not in Kozhikode city itself but at Mayiladumkunnu, ~10 km away (address: Mayiladumkunnu, Mayanad P.O., Kozhikode 673008). The shrine is dedicated to Lord Murugan as Dhandayudhapani Swami, and its architecture is said to mirror the famed Pazhani Murugan Temple of Tamil Nadu. Tradition holds the hilltop shrine is about 500 years old (verify - no documented founding date found). Local legend tells of Sri Babaji reviving the dying Saptaparni (Alstonia scholaris) tree beside the sanctum, which is now venerated. It offers panoramic views of the surrounding hills and is also listed as a tourist viewpoint. The temple runs charitable and community activities alongside daily worship.

name: Mel Pazhani Murugan Temple
town_description: Kozhikode (Calicut) is a major coastal city in northern Kerala and the historic seat of the Zamorin dynasty. A famed medieval trading port of the Malabar coast, it is known for its spices, beaches, and vibrant food culture. Mayiladumkunnu, the hill that holds the temple, lies about 10 km from the city centre amid dense foliage.

travel.railway: Kozhikode railway station, about 10 km away
travel.road: Atop Mayiladumkunnu hill, reached by road via Mayanad/Meenchanda; taxi or private vehicle recommended; about 10 km from Kozhikode city

visitor_information.best_time: November to March; Thaipoosam (January-February) is the grandest occasion
